## Gatun Lake: where the Panama Canal meets tropical forest

Gatun Lake (Lago Gatún) lies in central Panama and forms an essential waterway within the [Panama Canal](/panama/place/panama-canal/). For ships, it is part of the interoceanic route; for travellers, it is a chance to see huge vessels against a background of forested islands and spend time on the water away from the city's waterfront.

Gatun is unlike a natural lake. It was created during construction of the canal when the Chagres River was dammed. The lowlands flooded and the tops of former hills became islands. Today's landscape therefore combines shipping channels, wooded shores and quieter areas visited by small excursion boats.

## Why the Panama Canal depends on the lake

According to the Panama Canal Authority, the lake's water level is about 26 metres above sea level. Locks raise vessels to this height so they can travel across part of the lake before descending through another set of locks. Water enters the lock chambers by gravity, making the condition of the watershed crucial to the canal's operation.

The reservoir was created in the early twentieth century as part of the interoceanic waterway and was once among the world's largest artificial lakes. Its role now extends beyond shipping: water from the basin also supplies populated areas and serves other needs. The level depends on rainfall and management of the water system, another reason for visitors to consider the season and navigation conditions.

At the [Miraflores Locks](/panama/place/miraflores-locks/) and [Agua Clara Locks](/panama/place/agua-clara-locks/), you can watch vessels rise and descend. The experience on Gatun is different: ships move across open water with forest and small islands nearby. The two kinds of visit complement each other.

## Boat trips, islands and wildlife

One way to discover the lake is by small boat. The route may follow calm waters beside forested banks and islands while cargo ships remain in the main shipping lanes. You must never approach the channel or a large ship independently: the boat captain's instructions and navigation rules govern movement.

Around [Monkey Island](/panama/place/monkey-island-gatun/), you may look out for capuchins, howler monkeys and other forest animals, as well as waterbirds and birds living near the shore. Sightings vary with the time of day, weather and animal behaviour. Even in an area known for monkeys, a particular species cannot be guaranteed. Feeding wild animals or trying to lure them to the boat disrupts responsible wildlife watching.

The scientific value of these forests is illustrated by Barro Colorado Island. It became an island when the reservoir filled and is now known for long-term tropical research by the Smithsonian Institution. Visits to this research area are subject to special rules; an ordinary Gatun Lake boat excursion does not automatically include access to Barro Colorado.

## Combining Gatun Lake with nearby attractions

The lake fits naturally into a central Panama itinerary. [Panama City](/panama/place/panama-city/) is a common starting base, from which travellers can head towards Gatun and continue exploring the canal's history and the Caribbean coast.

On the [seven-day “All of Panama” tour](/panama/tour/panama-national-parks-islands-valleys/), one day combines [Soberanía National Park](/panama/place/soberania-national-park/), the lake, [San Lorenzo Fort](/panama/place/san-lorenzo-fort/) and [Agua Clara Locks](/panama/place/agua-clara-locks/). This sequence reveals both forest and shipping infrastructure but leaves less free time at each stop.

The [12-day Panama itinerary](/panama/tour/luxury-panama-12-days/) includes Gatun on a separate day with Monkey Island and San Lorenzo Fort. The exact transfers, excursions and meals depend on the selected tour's terms rather than on the lake visit itself. If birdwatching and forest life matter most, agree in advance how much of the day will be devoted to the boat trip.

## Seasons, equipment and safety

Central Panama has relatively drier and wetter periods. Showers are more likely during the rainy season and visibility on the water can change; in drier months strong sunshine requires protection even when the sky is cloudy. Boat excursions are arranged according to weather and the availability of a safe route.

Bring a hat, light covering clothing, sunscreen, drinking water and a waterproof case for your phone. Binoculars are useful for birdwatching. When boarding and underway, follow the captain's instructions and use the prescribed safety equipment. Observe wildlife from a distance.

The lake appeals both to nature lovers and travellers interested in understanding how the canal works. Compare programmes in the [Panama tour catalogue](/panama/tour/), or explore the [Wildlife and Nature section](/interests/wildlife/) for journeys focusing on national parks and animal observation.

## Frequently asked questions about Gatun Lake

### Is Gatun Lake natural or artificial?

Artificial. It formed when the Chagres River was dammed during construction of the Panama Canal, leaving former hilltops as islands.

### Can you see large ships from a boat?

Yes. Ocean-going vessels cross the lake. How close an excursion boat can travel to the shipping lane depends on the route and safety rules.

### Are monkey sightings guaranteed?

No. The animals move freely through the forest, and sightings depend on location, time and weather.

### Can you visit Barro Colorado on a regular excursion?

No. Visiting the scientific research area requires special arrangements under Smithsonian Institution rules. An ordinary lake excursion does not include access to the research station.

[Gatun Lake](/panama/place/gatun-lake/) is the central reservoir of the [Panama Canal](/panama/place/panama-canal/) water system. From a boat, you can see wooded islands, lush banks and ships travelling between the oceans. A visitor excursion usually focuses on the lake's natural surroundings rather than crossing the entire canal and its locks.

Our selection contains {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with Gatun on their main itineraries. Choose according to how many days you can spend in Panama and what else you would like to experience.

**[“Panama City and Gamboa: Canal, Forest and Emberá in 6 Days”](/panama/tour/panama-city-gamboa-6-days/)** is suitable for travellers seeking a compact introduction to the country's nature. **[“Luxury Panama: 12 Days of VIP Travel”](/panama/tour/luxury-panama-12-days/)** visits the lake as early as day 2. After the boat excursion and San Lorenzo Fort, the journey continues into other parts of Panama, with time on the Pacific coast, the Boquete mountain region and Caribbean islands. ## Comparing Gatun Lake itineraries

| Tour | How the lake is visited |
|---|---|
| [6 days: Panama City and Gamboa](/panama/tour/panama-city-gamboa-6-days/) | Day 5: boat, Monkey Island |
| [7 days: All of Panama](/panama/tour/panama-national-parks-islands-valleys/) | Day 5: lake, San Lorenzo, Agua Clara |
| [12 days: Luxury Panama](/panama/tour/luxury-panama-12-days/) | Day 2: lake, wildlife, fortress |

### 6 days: the lake after walking through the forest

On the six-day trip, the nature experience begins on the [Chagres River](/panama/place/chagres-river/) with a visit to an [Emberá community](/panama/place/embera-chagres-community/). Travellers then spend two nights in [Gamboa](/panama/place/gamboa/). A separate day is devoted to the trails of [Soberanía National Park](/panama/place/soberania-national-park/) and the [Panama Rainforest Discovery Center](/panama/place/panama-rainforest-discovery-center/).

Only after exploring the forest on land do travellers board a boat for an excursion on Gatun Lake and towards Monkey Island. This sequence suits nature lovers who want to experience the forest both from the ground and from the water. In the second half of day 5, the trip returns to Panama City. **The two nights in Gamboa come before the lake outing; after Gatun, accommodation is in the capital.**

The itinerary includes a standalone excursion, [“Gatun Lake and Monkey Island by Boat”](/panama/gatun-lake/gatun-lake-monkey-island-boat/). Its description defines what the boat trip includes; the name does not imply visits to every other island on the lake.

### 7 days: lake, fortress and locks in one day

The seven-day programme visits [Panama City](/panama/place/panama-city/), [Chagres National Park](/panama/place/chagres-national-park/) and [Taboga Island](/panama/place/taboga-island/) before a fifth day devoted to the canal.

The group first travels towards [Soberanía](/panama/place/soberania-national-park/). A boat carries travellers along the Chagres onto the Panama Canal waters and towards the wooded islands. In their natural habitat, capuchins, howler monkeys, tamarins, birds and other animals may be encountered, though seeing any particular species cannot be guaranteed.

The journey then continues towards historic [San Lorenzo Fort](/panama/place/san-lorenzo-fort/) on the Caribbean side and the modern [Agua Clara Locks](/panama/place/agua-clara-locks/). This is a good choice for visitors hoping to see the waterway, nature and fortifications within a single day. It is a fairly full schedule with no independent overnight stay at the lake.

### 12 days: a boat excursion before a longer journey

On the [12-day tour of Panama](/panama/tour/luxury-panama-12-days/), Gatun falls on **day 2**. The boat travels across the lake near commercial ships. The excursion includes opportunities to observe wildlife, including monkeys, followed in the afternoon by [San Lorenzo](/panama/place/san-lorenzo-fort/).

Afterwards the destination changes. Travellers head towards [David](/panama/place/david/), the coast near [Boca Chica](/panama/place/boca-chica/), then [Boquete](/panama/place/boquete/) and [Barú Volcano](/panama/place/baru-volcano/). Following the highlands and coffee plantations, the journey continues to the Caribbean Sea.

Choose this option if Gatun is only the first memorable stop on a broader exploration of Panama. A longer total journey does not necessarily mean more hours on the lake than on a shorter trip. Compare the actual sequence of days rather than the programme's total duration.

## What will you see on Gatun Lake?

Gatun Lake formed during construction of the Panama Canal and is a major part of its water system. Forest surrounds the reservoir, while some islands are hilltops left above water after it filled. From an excursion boat, you can see how closely one of the world's busiest maritime routes passes tropical forest.

Around [Monkey Island](/panama/place/monkey-island-gatun/), wild animals live freely. In favourable conditions, monkeys and birds can be seen along the banks and branches, with huge ships in the background as they travel along the main channel. The boat may approach the islands, but that does not imply landing on each of them.

**A Gatun Lake trip differs from a visit to the locks.** At [Miraflores](/panama/place/miraflores-locks/) or [Agua Clara](/panama/place/agua-clara-locks/), you observe the chambers and gates raising or lowering ships. On the lake, travellers move among the islands and experience the canal as a large body of water. An excursion-boat trip on Gatun is not the same as a full transit between the oceans.

For a broader choice of canal attractions, explore [tours including the Panama Canal](/panama/place/panama-canal/tour/). This selection concentrates on itineraries where **the lake itself is confirmed**.

## Gamboa, Gatun and Agua Clara: how the places relate

[Gamboa](/panama/place/gamboa/) is a departure area for boat excursions in the canal's central section. [Gatun](/panama/place/gatun-lake/) is the lake where the excursions take place. [Agua Clara](/panama/place/agua-clara-locks/) is a separate lock complex towards the Atlantic, reached by land.

The locations are linked geographically and thematically, but they are not interchangeable. A tour with a boat trip on the lake does not necessarily include Agua Clara, and a tour visiting the locks does not automatically head to Monkey Island.

To choose a route, consider three questions: Is the boat excursion mandatory? Is an island stop scheduled? How much time remains for surrounding natural areas? On these criteria, the six-day itinerary focuses on nature, the seven-day option combines canal infrastructure and historical sites, while the twelve-day programme places Gatun within a wider holiday through several parts of Panama.

## Practical advice before going out on the lake

The lake has a tropical climate. Wear a hat, sunscreen and light clothing that covers your shoulders. Keep your phone, documents and camera protected from spray. If an outing involves landing or walking near a forested shore, non-slip footwear is useful.

There can be heavy showers and waves caused by passing ships. The exact route depends on local conditions, so follow the captain's instructions and use the safety equipment provided. Never feed monkeys or approach them too closely for a photograph.

When planning the day, allow for departure from the capital, boarding and onward transfers. The seven-day itinerary includes a fortress and locks after the boat trip, limiting time for extra stops. On the six-day itinerary you return to Panama City after the excursion; on the twelve-day one, the lake trip is also paired with a visit to San Lorenzo.

## Which tour should you choose?

**6 days** if you want to combine Gatun with forest trails and two nights in Gamboa.

**7 days** if you want to see how shipping, nature, historic fortresses and modern Panama Canal locks come together.

**12 days** if you want a longer journey through Panama, starting with a lake excursion and continuing to beaches, coffee plantations and the mountains.

Prices and conditions are given on the individual tour pages. A VIP title does not guarantee a separate private boat or a particular service package on Gatun. Check the actual route, included-services list and guiding conditions.

## Frequently asked questions about Gatun Lake tours

### How many Ada Tours itineraries include Gatun?

The current number is shown in the catalogue: {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. The selection is calculated from active programmes with the lake on the main route and changes when the catalogue is updated.

### Can visitors see monkeys?

Yes, the itineraries include a visit towards Monkey Island or a boat excursion offering opportunities to observe wildlife. Sightings depend on animal behaviour; no number or species can be guaranteed.

### Does the tour pass through the locks?

A lake trip alone does not mean transiting the locks. The seven-day itinerary includes a separate visit to [Agua Clara](/panama/place/agua-clara-locks/), while the other programmes describe their lock visits in the relevant days. A complete canal transit should never be assumed.

### Which tour includes an overnight stay in Gamboa?

[“Panama City and Gamboa”](/panama/tour/panama-city-gamboa-6-days/) includes two nights at Gamboa Rainforest Resort. On the other itineraries shown, visiting the lake does not automatically involve an overnight stay at that hotel.

### How do I choose between 6-, 7- and 12-day trips?

Compare the required lake visits and the attractions that follow. The six-day trip offers a base for exploring nature in Gamboa; the seven-day trip combines the waterway with canal history; the twelve-day trip continues west across Panama. They also differ in accommodation and total duration.

The [Panama tour catalogue](/panama/tour/) compares these journeys with other routes around the country, while the [Gatun Lake page](/panama/place/gatun-lake/) introduces the destination itself.

## Gulf of Chiriquí Marine National Park: islands on Panama's Pacific coast

On [Panama's](/panama/) western coast, the Gulf of Chiriquí Marine National Park protects forested islands, small beaches and marine ecosystems. Visitors come for boat outings, snorkelling, wildlife observation and a few hours beside the water. Unlike a coastal resort on the mainland, the experience is centred on travelling between islands, with plans determined by sea conditions and where landings are permitted.

The park lies in Chiriquí Province, and boat trips often depart from Boca Chica. Exploring this Pacific coast fits well after city days in Panama City or alongside the mountain portion of a journey through the country's west. Other landscapes and routes appear in the [Panama tour catalogue](/panama/tour/).

## Which islands and natural features can you see?

### Parida, Gámez and Bolaños

Parida, Gámez and Bolaños are among the best-known islands visited on excursions in the marine park. Some shorelines are forested and rocky; others feature pale sandy coves. The actual islands, stops and beaches depend on the boat route, sea conditions and rules for visiting the protected area.

Mangrove habitats shelter young fish and many other marine organisms. Near the islands you can find coral communities, rocky seabeds and different conditions for snorkelling. These habitats provide distinct experiences in one outing: a trip alongside mangroves is not the same as snorkelling at an appropriate reef, and a beach stop does not guarantee clear underwater visibility.

### Marine animals and birds

Dolphins and seabirds may be seen in the Gulf of Chiriquí. Humpback whales visit the region during their migration; Panama's tourism portal identifies **July–October** as the principal whale-watching season. Even then, sightings depend on the animals and conditions at sea, so choosing dates within the season is more realistic than expecting a guaranteed encounter.

Scuba diving and snorkelling require different preparation. With a mask and snorkel, currents, waves and visibility at the chosen island are important. Scuba additionally depends on participants' qualifications, equipment and the instructor's decision. Explore the [diving section](/interests/diving/) for different formats; the specific excursion determines which services are included.

## How to reach the marine park

The usual departure point is **Boca Chica**, on the Pacific coast. Travellers reach it by road from David; those coming from Panama City may fly domestically to David before transferring by land. At Boca Chica, a boat takes visitors to the islands. Travel time and the possibility of landing vary by island, weather and programme.

For a one-day excursion, allow sufficient time for the return journey. The sea can be calm in the morning and rougher later; the boat operator chooses safe approaches and may change the order of stops. Boat trips, mainland transfers and diving cannot automatically be regarded as included in every tour that mentions the Gulf of Chiriquí.

## When to visit and what to bring

The period with less rainfall on Panama's Pacific coast generally falls in northern winter and early spring. During wetter months the islands remain green, but showers, waves and water conditions have a stronger influence on activities. For whale watching, the migration season matters most; for a beach day, check the forecast and marine conditions immediately before departure.

Bring sun-protective clothing, a hat, water, shoes suitable for boarding a boat and a waterproof phone case. For snorkelling, ask whether equipment is supplied and whether the site is suitable for children and less confident swimmers. Protected islands should not be treated as places where landing or camping is permitted anywhere.

## Combining the Gulf of Chiriquí with other regions

The marine park complements journeys through Panama's different landscapes. Visitors can first explore Chiriquí's mountains, then leave cooler elevations for the coast. The [“Panama – Costa Rica – Nicaragua” itinerary](/multi-country/tour/panama-costa-rica-nicaragua/) includes a stop at Gulf of Chiriquí Marine National Park. It is a specific multi-country journey, with marine activities and participation conditions determined by the actual programme.

For seaside relaxation, compare [Panama beach holidays](/interests/beach-holidays/tours/panama/) by stop duration and number of transfers. Wildlife enthusiasts may prefer the [Panama nature travel selection](/interests/wildlife/tours/panama/). Whether to choose a short boat outing or an overnight stay on the coast depends chiefly on how long you want to enjoy the islands.

## Frequently asked questions about the Gulf of Chiriquí Marine Park

### Can you reach the park without a boat?

The principal island excursions require a boat. Boca Chica can be reached by road, but boats carry travellers from the mainland docks to the islands.

### Are the Gulf of Chiriquí and Coiba National Park the same place?

No. Both are on Panama's Pacific coast, but **Gulf of Chiriquí Marine National Park and Coiba National Park are separate protected areas**. They should not be merged into one excursion because of their coastal location.

### When can humpback whales be seen?

Usually from July to October. It is a seasonal opportunity, not a guarantee of seeing a whale on a given day.

### Can I visit for just one day?

Yes. One-day island excursions are available around Boca Chica. For a more relaxed exploration of several coastal areas, allocate more time; the actual stops and return depend on weather and the agreed itinerary.

## Which tours visit Gulf of Chiriquí Marine National Park?

[Gulf of Chiriquí Marine National Park](/panama/place/gulf-of-chiriqui-national-marine-park/) is off the Pacific coast of Chiriquí Province. Forested islands, light sandy beaches, mangroves and coral ecosystems make it an important marine nature destination in western Panama.

Our selection contains {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with the marine park in their main itineraries. The journeys devote different amounts of time to the coast and continue in different directions.

**[“Best of Panama 2023”](/panama/tour/best-of-panama-2023/)** is an **11-day** single-country tour. Its route connects [Panama City](/panama/place/panama-city/), the Gulf of Chiriquí, mountain [Boquete](/panama/place/boquete/), [Barú Volcano](/panama/place/baru-volcano/) and [Bocas del Toro](/panama/place/bocas-del-toro/) on the Caribbean coast. The marine stop falls on day 4.

**[“Panama – Costa Rica – Nicaragua”](/multi-country/tour/panama-costa-rica-nicaragua/)** is a **13-day** journey through three Central American countries. Day 5 is specifically devoted to the national marine park, after which travellers explore Costa Rica's nature and Nicaragua's historic cities.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_luchshee_v_paname,tour_source_panama_kosta_rika_nikaragua}}

Both routes include a visit to the marine park, but **the islands where boats land and the precise water activities are determined by the programme**. The presence of sea and reefs does not imply that scuba diving, deep-sea fishing or every island visit is included for every participant.

## How do the two itineraries differ?

| Route | Day in Chiriquí |
|---|---|
| [11 days in Panama](/panama/tour/best-of-panama-2023/) | Day 4, after the flight to David |
| [13 days through three countries](/multi-country/tour/panama-costa-rica-nicaragua/) | Day 5, a separate marine outing |

### “Best of Panama”: the coast after the capital

The opening days take place in [Panama City](/panama/place/panama-city/) and nature areas of central Panama. The programme includes an introduction to the canal and a visit to [Chagres National Park](/panama/place/chagres-national-park/) to meet an Emberá community.

On day 4, an **early flight from Albrook Airport to [David](/panama/place/david/)**, the administrative centre of Chiriquí Province, is scheduled. After arrival, travellers transfer to the gulf area. The itinerary specifies accommodation at **Bocas del Mar 4-star hotel**. Relaxation and possible island trips depend on the ocean and the day's schedule. A visit to the marine park is part of the programme, but scuba diving is not specified as a mandatory activity.

The following day, travellers head from [Boca Chica](/panama/place/boca-chica/) towards [Boquete](/panama/place/boquete/) for canopy activities and a coffee plantation. Later the group visits [Barú Volcano](/panama/place/baru-volcano/) and the Caribbean Sea.

This choice suits visitors wanting to experience several sides of Panama: Pacific islands, cooler mountain slopes, coffee-growing areas and the very different nature of the Caribbean coast.

### “Panama – Costa Rica – Nicaragua”: a full day in the marine park

On the 13-day trip, the Panamanian stage begins with the capital, [Chagres](/panama/place/chagres-national-park/) and cultural visits. The route then heads to Chiriquí Province. **Day 5** is given over to the national marine park: islands and beaches of the western Pacific coast. The tour explicitly states that the ability to explore the islands depends on calm sea conditions.

The following day is already devoted to continuing towards Costa Rica. Travellers then visit the natural regions of Manuel Antonio, Monteverde and Arenal, and finish in Nicaragua. Compared with the eleven-day itinerary, this trip includes more countries, borders and types of protected areas.

If **a dedicated day beside the ocean** is important, the thirteen-day trip allocates a clearer place to the park within the schedule. If you prefer more time in Panama combining the coast, mountain excursions and the Caribbean Sea, the eleven-day option is more suitable.

## Where is the marine park and how do visitors reach it?

The Gulf of Chiriquí is on Panama's western Pacific coast. [Boca Chica](/panama/place/boca-chica/) is a convenient departure point for many island trips. It can be reached by road from [David](/panama/place/david/), after which passengers board a small boat. David itself can be reached from the capital by road or domestic flight; the flight is specified on the eleven-day tour.

The best-known islands in this area include Parida, Gámez and Bolaños, as well as other beaches and mangrove shores. The regional tourism map covers more than any single excursion. **Neither of the two published tours explicitly guarantees landing on Parida, Gámez or Bolaños by name.** Do not choose a trip on the assumption that all three must be included in one day.

[Boquete](/panama/place/boquete/) and [Barú Volcano](/panama/place/baru-volcano/) lie in the mountains of western Panama. The weather and activities are different there: trails, coffee plantations and cooler highlands. They fit well with the coast on a longer itinerary, but form a separate travel stage.

## What will you see on the Gulf of Chiriquí islands?

Forested islands, sandy bays, rocky shores and coral reefs occur here. Mangroves support coastal ecosystems, while the sea is habitat for birds, fish and other wildlife. During boat outings, the changing shorelines between islands are especially noticeable.

In favourable conditions, travellers can relax on a beach, swim and observe underwater life. Snorkelling, scuba diving and sport fishing are also offered in the wider region. **These are characteristics of the destination, not an automatic package of included services on every Ada Tours tour.** A particular dive, fishing excursion or island visit requires an explicitly confirmed product and suitable conditions.

Do not confuse the Gulf of Chiriquí with [Bocas del Toro](/panama/place/bocas-del-toro/). The former lies on the Pacific Ocean, the latter on the Caribbean Sea. Both are known for islands and seaside holidays, but distances, natural conditions and transfers between them matter. The eleven-day itinerary visits these places on different days.

### The marine park and Coiba National Park

Several protected marine areas lie off Panama's Pacific coast, including Coiba National Park. Its name often appears in descriptions of the country's western region, but **Coiba and Gulf of Chiriquí Marine National Park are distinct protected areas**.

A visit to the Gulf of Chiriquí does not automatically include travel to Coiba, its dive sites or a marine expedition. If an island is absent from the itinerary, its visit cannot be considered mandatory. This distinction is especially important when choosing a trip based on photographs of seascapes.

## When to plan the marine portion

Island excursions depend on ocean conditions: strong winds, waves or showers can restrict boating and landing at particular beaches. Panama's western coast has relatively drier and wetter periods, but conditions on the actual day matter more than a seasonal label.

Before travelling, check the current rules for visiting protected areas, permitted boat routes and weather restrictions. Panama's Ministry of the Environment sometimes temporarily restricts access to national parks during adverse weather warnings. A generally accessible protected area is therefore not necessarily open in all its parts on every date.

Allow time for the transfer from David to the dock and for boarding. On the eleven-day tour, day 4 already includes a domestic flight and a road transfer, so lengthy additional water activities should not automatically be added. On the thirteen-day itinerary the marine park has its own day, though the precise boat route still depends on conditions.

## What to bring to the islands

For a warm coastal excursion, bring a hat, water, sunscreen and shoes suitable for boarding and disembarking from a boat. Sun-protective clothing helps during long periods in open water. Keep phones and documents in waterproof pouches.

If snorkelling is planned, check in advance whether a mask, snorkel and life jacket are supplied by the specific operator. Swimming confidently in a pool is different from spending time in the open ocean. In rough seas, staying ashore or adjusting the water programme at the captain's discretion may be safer.

Do not leave litter, damage coral or disturb wild animals for photographs in the marine park. Observing the protected area's rules is part of a safe trip, even if the excursion feels like a simple beach holiday.

## Which tour is right for you?

**For a trip entirely within Panama**, choose [“Best of Panama 2023”](/panama/tour/best-of-panama-2023/). It combines the Gulf of Chiriquí with Boquete, Barú and Bocas del Toro. It is suitable for those wanting to compare Panama's two coasts and its mountains.

**For a journey through three Central American countries**, choose [“Panama – Costa Rica – Nicaragua”](/multi-country/tour/panama-costa-rica-nicaragua/). The marine park is included before the border crossing, then the route continues through other natural regions. Decide according to your desired geography and readiness for international transfers.

Both journeys can be compared in the [Panama tour catalogue](/panama/tour/). Visitors choosing natural destinations in particular may also appreciate the [Gulf of Chiriquí Marine National Park page](/panama/place/gulf-of-chiriqui-national-marine-park/): it describes the protected area, while this article focuses on current travel programmes.

## Frequently asked questions

### Which Ada Tours itineraries include Gulf of Chiriquí Marine National Park?

This selection contains {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. It includes the [11-day Panama tour](/panama/tour/best-of-panama-2023/) and the [13-day trip through Panama, Costa Rica and Nicaragua](/multi-country/tour/panama-costa-rica-nicaragua/). Both list the park on their principal route.

### How much time is spent in the park?

The eleven-day itinerary visits the marine area on day 4 alongside a flight to David and a transfer to the coast. The thirteen-day itinerary gives the park its own day 5. The exact hours at sea are not a fixed common condition of both tours.

### Is scuba diving included?

The presence of coral reefs and diving opportunities in the Gulf of Chiriquí does not establish that dives are included in either tour's price. The programmes mention visiting islands, beaches and marine areas when weather permits. A specialist dive programme must be distinguished from swimming and snorkelling.

### Can the Gulf of Chiriquí be combined with Boquete?

Yes. The [11-day “Best of Panama” tour](/panama/tour/best-of-panama-2023/) continues from the coast to [Boquete](/panama/place/boquete/) and [Barú Volcano](/panama/place/baru-volcano/). The thirteen-day itinerary heads onward to Costa Rica and Nicaragua.

No. The marine park is a required geographical stop, but not every individual island is listed by name. The boat route depends on weather, protected-area regulations and the confirmed excursion.

### How is the Gulf of Chiriquí different from Bocas del Toro?

[The Gulf of Chiriquí](/panama/place/gulf-of-chiriqui-national-marine-park/) is in the Pacific Ocean, whereas [Bocas del Toro](/panama/place/bocas-del-toro/) lies in the Caribbean Sea. A trip through Panama can include both, but they are separate stages requiring transfers.

## Holandes Cays: remote San Blas islands for a yacht journey

The Holandes Cays (Cayos Holandeses, or Dutch Cays) are a group of small Caribbean islands within the [San Blas archipelago](/panama/place/san-blas-islands/) in Panama's Guna Yala territory. Travellers head here for white sandy shores, clear shallows, coral areas and anchorages among reefs. Their main distinction from a popular short trip to nearer San Blas islands is the distance and the way you travel: the Holandes Cays are best explored by yacht, moving between islands and spending the night on board.

This destination appeals to travellers wanting time beside the water, snorkelling and island scenery without urban infrastructure. The actual anchorage, landing and opportunity to swim depend on weather, sea conditions and the vessel's itinerary.

## Where are the Holandes Cays and why visit by yacht?

Holandes is one of the more remote groups within Guna Yala. The islands are protected by parts of a reef system, with sheltered shallow waters and deeper passages between them. A captain chooses the approach to an anchorage according to navigational conditions; an attractive beach view alone does not indicate safe water depth for a yacht.

Unlike a beach beside a road, these islands require a sea crossing. Its duration depends on the departure point, vessel and waves. Visitors should not plan the Holandes Cays as a guaranteed short stop from [Panama City](/panama/place/panama-city/). It is better to choose a route with a separate day allocated to the more distant part of the San Blas archipelago.

Guna Yala is governed by authorities of the Indigenous Guna people. Rules on visiting, navigation and using island facilities differ from those of an unrestricted public beach. Agree anchorages and landings with the crew and in accordance with local requirements.

## What can you do in the Holandes Cays?

### Snorkelling around the reef

Clear water offers views of reef areas and fish through a mask and snorkel wherever conditions are safe. Visibility changes after rain, in wind and rough seas, so even a well-known spot cannot be promised as ideal in every kind of weather. Use sun protection, never stand on living corals and follow the captain's instructions when entering the water.

Snorkelling and scuba diving are different activities. Scuba requires a confirmed diving programme, suitable site, equipment and appropriate preparation. The presence of a reef or an island anchorage does not by itself mean diving is included. Those interested in the activity can explore [diving journeys](/interests/diving/) and check the precise tour inclusions.

### Swimming in the shallows and relaxing on the islands

Some islands have shallow lagoons with sandy areas. For swimming, a safe entry point matters more than finding the whitest beach in a photo: tides, currents and conditions around the reef change. Outside palm-covered patches there is little shade on land, so drinking water and sun protection are essential.

Before choosing a route, ask whether it includes landing on a particular island or enjoying the beach from the yacht. Not every anchorage allows access to every shore, and visits to inhabited community areas must respect local rules.

### Fishing and a day at sea

On the [Ada Tours San Blas yacht itinerary](/panama/tour/panama-san-blas-luxury-yacht/), the Holandes day includes fishing, swimming and exploring the reefs. Whether fishing is allowed, which methods and areas are permitted, and any restrictions depend on local regulations and the agreed programme. A short opportunity to fish during a cruise is not equivalent to a specialist [fishing tour](/interests/fishing/).

## Holandes, Coco Bandero and Isla Perro: how do the stops differ?

Each island stage serves a different purpose. [Coco Bandero](/panama/place/coco-bandero-island/) is known for scenic little islands and shallow reefs. [Isla Perro](/panama/place/isla-perro/) on the yacht itinerary includes a chance to explore a sunken vessel underwater. [Turtle Island](/panama/place/turtle-island/) is listed as a separate stop for discovering local island life and nature.

Holandes offers a more remote stretch of sailing, focusing on an anchorage, the reef and a relaxed day by the sea. Consider these islands as consecutive stages if you want to discover different areas of San Blas. The activities listed belong to the specific Ada Tours itinerary; they are not an automatic package on every island excursion.

## Visiting Holandes on an Ada Tours itinerary

On the [eight-day Panama and San Blas yacht journey](/panama/tour/panama-san-blas-luxury-yacht/), the route begins near [Flamenco Island](/panama/place/flamenco-island/), travels through the [Panama Canal](/panama/place/panama-canal/) and Caribbean [Shelter Bay](/panama/place/shelter-bay/), then continues around the islands of Guna Yala. The Holandes day follows stops at Porvenir and Coco Bandero. Swimming, fishing, sea views and a barbecue beach stop are planned for that day.

The order matters: the yacht gradually reaches the more distant islands, giving travellers several different days at sea. Before booking, compare the day-by-day itinerary and the conditions on board. Allow time for weather-related changes during sea crossings, and discuss susceptibility to seasickness before making a reservation.

For swimming, bring shoes suitable for wet surfaces, covering sun-protective clothing, a mask if you prefer one and waterproof storage for documents. The precise equipment supplied by the crew is defined in the selected tour's conditions.

## Frequently asked questions about the Holandes Cays

### Can I visit the Holandes Cays on a day trip from Panama City?

Their distance and the sea crossing make this less convenient than visiting the nearer San Blas islands. A yacht itinerary with dedicated time in the Holandes Cays is more practical.

### Are the Holandes Cays good for snorkelling?

Yes. The area has reefs and shallow waters. Safety and visibility depend on weather, currents and the actual anchorage.

### Can I go scuba diving?

Only if a dive is specifically part of the agreed itinerary, with suitable conditions and equipment. Reefs beside the yacht do not establish that a scuba-diving service is included.

### How are the Holandes Cays different from San Blas?

[San Blas](/panama/place/san-blas-islands/) is the wider island archipelago. Holandes is a particular remote group within it. A tour advertised as “San Blas” does not necessarily include the Holandes Cays.
